release_published_at: resolved by uv from PyPI metadata on 2026-09-23; ml-explore/mlx-lm's newest tagged GitHub release at query time is v0.31.3 (published 2026-04-22T07:43:57Z per `gh api repos/ml-explore/mlx-lm/releases/latest`), but uv's dependency resolver does not select it for aarch64-apple-darwin / Python 3.12 or 3.13 (see results)

preregistration.expectation: `uv pip compile --python-platform aarch64-apple-darwin --generate-hashes` against a bare `mlx-lm` requirement will resolve and hash-lock a coherent, installable dependency set with no torch/CUDA packages (mlx-lm's dependency graph is CPU/Metal-only), and will pick the newest version compatible with the target platform/Python constraints -- which this check must confirm is not necessarily GitHub's 'latest release' tag.
preregistration.criteria: The generated lock file installs with `uv pip install --require-hashes` (checked by structure, not executed here since this host is x86_64 Linux, not macOS); it contains no torch/cuda* entries; and a second, independent `uv pip compile` run of the same input is byte-for-byte identical (deterministic resolution) so the CI job's redundant-compile diff check in hardware-profile-smoke.yml is meaningful rather than always failing.

acceptance_check_ref: None retained prior to this unit; this is this unit's first pin for mlx-lm. Forward acceptance is the macOS job in .github/workflows/hardware-profile-smoke.yml, not yet executed (requires a macos-15 runner).

uv pip compile /tmp/req.in --python-platform aarch64-apple-darwin --python-version 3.13 (unconstrained mlx-lm, to check whether 3.13 unlocks a newer resolution)
results: Unconstrained `uv pip compile` (no version pin in requirements.in) independently resolved mlx-lm==0.30.2 for both --python-version 3.12 and 3.13 targets on aarch64-apple-darwin, matching the explicit ==0.30.2 pin: uv's own resolver does not pick 0.31.3 for this platform/Python combination even when unconstrained.
PyPI's actual release list (fetched directly, not via GitHub) confirms 0.31.3 exists upstream (0.30.4...0.30.7, 0.31.0...0.31.3), so this is a resolver/metadata constraint, not a stale PyPI mirror.

gh api repos/ml-explore/mlx-lm/releases/latest: tag_name v0.31.3, published_at 2026-04-22T07:43:57Z -- recorded as the actual newest upstream release per the evidence-discipline instruction, even though this pin does not use it.
Generated lock file: 38 top-level+transitive packages, no torch/cuda* entries (verified by `grep '^torch' requirements.lock.txt` returning no match).

First attempt used `--emit-index-url -o <path>` and was NOT byte-identical across two runs to different output paths: the only diff was the autogenerated header comment line, which echoes the exact command including the -o value. Since the CI job's verify step always writes to a $RUNNER_TEMP path different from the committed file's path, that header line would have made the diff step fail unconditionally. Fixed by switching both the committed lock file and the workflow's regeneration step to `--no-header` (dropping `--emit-index-url`, which is not needed without the header); a second `--no-header` compile then produced a byte-identical file (verified with `diff -q`, exit 0).
limits: The resolution and hash generation were run on x86_64 Linux (this host) targeting aarch64-apple-darwin via uv's --python-platform cross-resolution; the lock file's actual installability with --require-hashes on a real macOS arm64 host is not yet verified by execution -- only by .github/workflows/hardware-profile-smoke.yml's macOS job, which this unit authored but did not run (no macOS host available here).

Root cause for why uv's resolver stops at 0.30.2 instead of 0.31.3 was not traced further (e.g. a stricter mlx or transformers dependency bound in 0.31.x); this receipt records the observation, not a diagnosed upstream reason.
'not_comparable' because there is no prior mlx-lm pin in this repository to compare against; this is a new addition, not a version-bump qualification of an existing pin.
